evidence_set: All 18 sought care for long-standing symptoms including nasal obstruction, nosebleeds and severe facial pain (facial pain in 3 of 18 by Table 1, p. 392); the commonest findings at the first visit were diffuse necrotising ulcers, extensive crusting and septal perforation; clinically, destruction of the septum and inferior turbinates was found in all (imaging: inferior turbinate in 12 of 16), extending in more severe cases to the middle and superior turbinates and the lateral nasal wall, entirely absorbed in 3; hard and soft palate perforations were present in 2 at the first visit and appeared during follow-up in 3 more. The authors say the lesions gave rise to difficulty swallowing and nasal reflux (numbers not given) and substantially affected quality of life, which was not measured.

Figure 3 prints, for the lesion group, septum 100%, inferior turbinate 61%, middle turbinate 33%, superior turbinate 16%, lateral wall 11% and floor or palate 28% (septum 12% for Wegener granulomatosis). Except for the septum these do not match the imaging counts in the text and Table 3 (12, 10, 2, 5 and 4 of 16: 75%, 62.5%, 12.5%, 31.25% and 25%), nor the clinical statement that the inferior turbinates were destroyed in all; only the 28% matches a stated count, the 5 of 18 with palate perforations at the first visit or during follow-up (27.8%, p. 393). The values are close to counts of 11, 6, 3, 2 and 5 out of 18 (61.1%, 33.3%, 16.7%, 11.1% and 27.8%; editors' arithmetic), which the paper does not explain. The claim uses the counts of 16 from the text and Table 3.

At presentation, lesions against Wegener granulomatosis: fever 0 of 18 against 13 of 21, weight loss 0 against 7, arthralgia or arthritis 0 against 7, lung involvement 0 against 12, ear involvement 0 against 7; haemoglobin 14.2 against 11.1 g/dL; CRP 12.2 ± 12 against 79.4 ± 73.7 mg/L, p = 0.002; ESR 31 ± 25 against 66 ± 41 mm/h, p = 0.009 (the table does not say whether ± is the SD). In the lesion group CRP was abnormal in 9 and ESR in 8 of 18, white cells raised in 5 and anaemia present in 2; liver and kidney tests were normal and hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV tests negative in all. All 21 with Wegener granulomatosis had crusting, 3 a septal perforation on examination, and none involvement of the turbinates, lateral wall or palate; systemic symptoms and blood changes were absent in only 2 of them.

44 biopsies from the 18 people with lesions (1 to 16 per person) and 29 from the 21 with Wegener granulomatosis: nonspecific changes in 19 of 44 against 7 of 29; among biopsies with significant abnormalities (25 and 22), perivenulitis 24 against 22, microabscesses in vessel walls 10 against 11, thrombi 7 against 5, leukocytoclastic vasculitis 7 against 14 (p = 0.02 per biopsy; per person 6 of 18 against 9 of 21, printed p = 0.11, editors' Fisher exact test p = 0.74), single giant cells or granulomas 0 against 9 and deeply located necrosis 0 against 19 (both p < 0.001). These extravascular changes were the only features found only in Wegener granulomatosis.

evidence_set: Systematic review and network meta-analysis of double-blind randomized trials of at least 1 week of oral ADHD medicines given alone (amphetamines including lisdexamfetamine, methylphenidate including dexmethylphenidate, and five others) against each other or placebo, searched to 7 April 2017 without language restriction; for 83% of trials, additional data and information not reported in the full-text paper were used. 133 trials: 81 in children and adolescents (5 to 17 years), 51 in adults and 1 in both, with 14,346 children and adolescents and 10,296 adults. Primary outcomes at the time closest to 12 weeks: clinician-rated change in core symptoms (and teacher ratings in children and adolescents), analysed in 10,068 children and adolescents and 8131 adults, and leaving a trial because of any side effect, analysed in 11,018 and 5362; weight and blood pressure secondary.

evidence_set: 337,919 starters (119,708 methylphenidate, 218,211 amphetamine; 232,096 person-years); after matching 221,846 (110,923 per group; 143,286 person-years; maximal standardized mean difference 0.02; mean age 17.0 to 17.1; 37.2% to 37.5% female; recorded alcohol use disorder 1.1% to 1.5% and cannabis use disorder 1.0% to 1.4%). 343 psychotic episodes (2.4 per 1000 person-years): 106 (0.10%) after methylphenidate and 237 (0.21%) after amphetamine; 1.78 against 2.83 episodes per 1000 person-years of drug exposure; pooled hazard ratio 1.65 (95% CI 1.31 to 2.09), prespecified as the primary analysis before unblinding of exposure status. Full unmatched cohort: 120 (0.10%) against 429 (0.20%); unadjusted HR 1.44 (1.17 to 1.77); multivariable adjusted 1.55 (1.25 to 1.92). Median time from the first dispensing to the episode 128 days (IQR 48 to 333).

evidence_set: The authors leave open whether the background characteristics that distinguish the returnees from the typical person addicted to narcotics in the United States, or the change in the social setting of use between Vietnam and the United States, explains the high remission; they do not know how much the short tour of duty contributed; they judge concealment unlikely (the men's candour, their free discussion of drug use in Vietnam, a low rate of urine specimens positive for opiates, high interview completion); they name Vietnam as a locale atypical in danger and in the quality, price and availability of its drugs, and the sample as homogeneous in age, sex, occupation and period, so the findings may not apply elsewhere; and new cases emerged throughout the period after return.
